newsitem.title: UK: Skilful beet storage factor in bumper UK sugar crop.
newsitem.headline: Skilful beet storage factor in bumper UK sugar crop.

text.p: Storage management by Britain's 9,300 sugar beet growers was probably the best ever in 1996/97 despite freezing temperatures and technical problems, the Sugar Beet Review said on Monday.

"They displayed considerable skill in the way in which they stored and protected their crop this year, despite one of the most sustained periods of freezing temperatures in recent memory," the Review's spring edition said.
The severe weather experienced in January was the coldest since 1987, the Review said.
The Sugar Beet Review is published quarterly by British Sugar plc.

Last month a British Sugar spokesman said Britain produced a record 1.48 million tonnes of sugar in white value terms from its 1996/97 beet crop, around 1,000 tonnes up on the previous record in 1992/93.

"There were some serious technical problems at the beginning and end of the campaign but despite this, factory staff achieved record factory throughputs and turned in a highly credible aggregate performance," the Review said.
It did not give details of the technical problems.
A total 475,000 loads of beet were delivered to British Sugar's nine factories in the 1996/97 campaign and less than two loads in every 1,000 were rejected due to frost damage, it added.
